cues.en: Or rather graves as it would have been pronounced in the original French. You see, the grav was the original name for the base unit of mass in the metric system, which became the system internationale dunite or SI units. In 1793,
cues.zh: 或者说，按法语原音应该读作“grav”。你看，grav是公制中质量基本单位的最初名称，后来演变为国际单位制，即SI单位。1793年，

cues.en: a commission which included notable scientist and aristocrat, Antoine Lavoisier,
cues.zh: 一个包括著名科学家和贵族安托万·拉瓦锡在内的委员会，

cues.en: defined the base unit of mass as the weight of a cubic decimeter of water at the melting temperature of ice. Essentially, just a liter of ice water.
cues.zh: 将质量基本单位定义为一立方分米的水在冰的熔点时的重量。本质上，就是一升冰水。

cues.en: The name grav came from the Latin gravitas,
cues.zh: grav这个名字来自拉丁语gravitas，

cues.en: meaning weight,

cues.en: but it wasn't to last.

cues.en: It sounded too similar to the aristocratic title, graf, which is the equivalent of an earl or a count. And with the French Revolution in full swing, with a rallying cry of equality for all, you couldn't exactly have one unit nobler than the others.
cues.zh: 它听起来太像贵族头衔graf，相当于伯爵。而且当时法国大革命正酣，口号是人人平等，你不可能让某个单位比其他单位更高贵。

cues.en: At this, Lavoisier lost his head,

cues.en: literally.
cues.zh: 是真的掉了。

cues.en: Not because he helped devise one of the greatest systems of measurement of all time, but because he was collecting taxes as a nobleman.
cues.zh: 不是因为他帮助设计了史上最伟大的计量体系之一，而是因为他作为贵族在收税。

cues.en: So things really were grave.
cues.zh: 所以事情真的很严重。

cues.en: The new republican government believed a grav would be too big for the things they wanted to measure anyway. And so they settled on a gram, which was just a thousandth of a grav.
cues.zh: 新的共和政府认为，grav对他们想测量的东西来说太大了。于是他们定了克，也就是grav的千分之一。

cues.en: But soon, they realized that a gram was too small, and so they returned to the grav. But since they couldn't call it that,
cues.zh: 但很快他们发现克太小了，于是又回到grav。但既然不能这么叫，

cues.en: they invented the kilogram,

cues.en: a thousand grams.

cues.en: And that is why out of the seven base SI units, the kilogram is the only one to have a prefix in its name.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么在国际单位制的七个基本单位中，千克是唯一一个名称里带前缀的。

cues.en: the kilogram definition was refined to be the mass of a liter of water at four degrees Celsius, the temperature at which it is densest.

cues.en: But water itself is obviously not the most sensible thing to use as a mass standard.
